120 minutes for everything you submit, including your video, as stated on the cover.

### The situation

Marsh & Colby is a mid-market commercial insurance brokerage, forty-some employees, three regional offices. Their underwriting assistants spend a meaningful part of each day reconciling policy documents against a coverage checklist before a policy can be bound. Ajaia is three weeks into a discovery engagement to design a tool that speeds this up. The stakeholder sponsor, Owen Restrepo, Director of Operations, has a feature list he is confident about. You have also interviewed two underwriting assistants and pulled a short description of how they actually use their current tool, a checklist spreadsheet called Bindwise. Owen has not seen the interview transcripts yet.

You are the Design Lead on this engagement. Your job in this pack is to figure out what Marsh & Colby's underwriting assistants actually need, design the ideal solution, and be ready to defend it to Owen when what you show him does not match what he asked for.

**Binding a policy:** the final step where a checklist of coverage requirements is confirmed complete and the policy becomes active. Cannot happen if a required document is missing or a coverage limit does not match what the client requested.

### The materials

**Material 1. Interview transcript excerpt, Anika Shah, Underwriting Assistant, Springfield office, lightly condensed**

> **Interviewer:** Walk me through binding a policy on a normal day.
>
> **Anika:** So I pull up the submission in Bindwise, and I go line by line down the checklist. Certificate of insurance, loss runs, the coverage limits page, all of it. If something's missing I flag it and email the broker.
>
> **Interviewer:** What's the most annoying part of that process?
>
> **Anika:** Honestly the checklist itself is fine, I've used it forever, I know it cold. What I actually hate is when I have to go back and forth with a broker over email because a document doesn't match, like the coverage limit on the cert doesn't match what's on the application. That can take days waiting on a reply.
>
> **Interviewer:** If you could wave a wand and fix one thing about Bindwise, what would it be?
>
> **Anika:** Probably just make the checklist faster to fill out. Some kind of smart autofill would be nice.

**Material 2. Interview transcript excerpt, Colin Doyle, Underwriting Assistant, Hartford office, lightly condensed**

> **Interviewer:** Same question, walk me through a normal binding.
>
> **Colin:** Okay so I open the folder for the submission, and honestly the checklist part goes fast, I basically know it by memory at this point. The slow part is finding the actual documents. They come in from like four different places, broker email, the client portal, sometimes a fax, don't ask. I'm hunting through my inbox half the time just to find the loss runs.
>
> **Interviewer:** How often does a mismatch come up, like a coverage limit not matching between documents?
>
> **Colin:** Pretty often actually, maybe a third of submissions have something off. Usually small stuff, but I have to catch it or it comes back to bite us later.
>
> **Interviewer:** How do you catch those mismatches right now?
>
> **Colin:** I just read carefully. I've gotten fast at it. It's not really the bottleneck for me, finding the documents in the first place is the bottleneck.

**Material 3. Stakeholder wishlist, email from Owen Restrepo**

> **From:** Owen Restrepo, Director of Operations, Marsh & Colby
> **To:** You
> **Subject:** Feature list for the new tool
>
> Been thinking about this since our kickoff. Here's what I'd want to see in v1:

1. Smart autofill for the coverage checklist so the assistants don't have to type everything by hand.
2. A cleaner-looking interface than Bindwise, it looks like it's from 2009.
3. Some kind of AI chat assistant they can ask questions to.
4. Mobile access, in case someone needs to check something from home.

> Our assistants know the checklist inside and out so I don't think we need to touch that part much, more just make it faster and modernize the look. Let me know what you come up with.

**Material 4. Bindwise usage description, pulled from the platform's activity log for the two interviewed assistants, last 30 days, summarized in text**

> Anika's account: 61 submissions processed. Average time from opening a submission to flagging the first missing or mismatched item: 14 minutes. Of the 61, 23 were flagged for a coverage-limit mismatch between the certificate of insurance and the application. Time from flag to broker reply, when logged: median 2.1 days, with nine submissions taking longer than 4 days.
>
> Colin's account: 54 submissions processed. Average time from opening a submission to locating all required source documents: 11 minutes, compared to an average of 3 minutes to complete the checklist itself once documents are located. 17 of 54 submissions had at least one document arrive through a channel other than the client portal (email attachment or fax scan), each of which took longer to locate. Coverage-limit mismatches appeared on 19 of 54 submissions.

### Tasks

**Task 1. Synthesis and next questions** (suggested time: 35 minutes)

Using the materials given, write:

- What Marsh & Colby's underwriting assistants actually need, as distinct from what Owen's wishlist asks for. For each need you name, cite the specific evidence line it comes from.
- One clear statement of where the interview transcripts and the usage log agree, and one clear statement of where they do not.
- Up to four questions you would ask in the next round of interviews. For each, state what would change about your design depending on the answer.

**Task 2. Design the ideal solution** (suggested time: 55 minutes)

Design the two or three screens that matter most, based on your synthesis, not the wishlist. Submit a user journey plus wireframes or a clickable prototype, in any tool. Your design should:

- Address what your synthesis found, even where it departs from Owen's list.
- Show where a human has to check or approve something, and why that checkpoint is there.

**Task 3. AI Workflow Note** (suggested time: 10 minutes)

In a few sentences: which tasks above you used AI for, what you deliberately kept human, and one specific thing an AI tool got wrong or you chose not to use.

### Your video

One video (suggested time: 20 minutes inside the 120-minute window; aim for 5 to 10 minutes of recording). Screen plus camera. Present your solution as if to Owen, the client sponsor. Partway through, assume Owen interrupts to say: "Our users asked for the wishlist, why are you showing me something else?" Answer him on camera, in character, using your evidence. Close with who you are, why this role and why Ajaia, and your salary expectations for this role. Do not state your current compensation; we are not asking for it here or anywhere else in this process.
